text:
jordan: heads up — i opened a small PR to hoist provider blocks to root and pin module sources by digest. goal is to simplify module upgrades and make the lockfile deterministic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432

talia: nice. did you also regenerate .terraform.lock.hcl? we should be careful about provider version bumps on prod clusters.

jordan: yep, regen included. i ran terraform init && terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64 and committed the lockfile. note: we’re still on terraform 1.4 in CI; the lock format is compatible but double-checks welcome.

anya: quick q — are we keeping provider configs in modules or centralizing? last time we had some weird aliasing for aws.us-east-1.

jordan: centralizing. modules will be provider-agnostic (no provider blocks). root has the provider configs with aliases. example we added:
```
provider "aws" {
  region = var.region
}
provider "aws" {
  alias  = "us_east"
  region = "us-east-1"
}
```
modules reference providers via provider = { aws = aws.us_east } where needed.

mike: fwiw i tested a canary stack in staging with the new layout — plan looked clean except for one module that still declared a provider for k8s. i opened a tiny follow-up to strip it out.

paul: any secrets wiring changes? we have a few modules still reading plaintext from k8s manifests (mounting from secretsRef).

jordan: good point. part of this PR swaps the k8s manifests to use the vault-secrets-provider via CSI. example change in deployment.yaml:
```yaml
volumes:
  - name: vault-creds
    csi:
      driver: secrets-store.csi.k8s.io
      readOnly: true
      volumeAttributes:
        secretProviderClass: "redwood-vault"
```
and the module now expects a secret_store boolean instead of embedding secrets.

talia: does that require infra team to create the SecretProviderClass per-cluster?

jordan: yes — i added a small docs note in infra/README.md with the steps to create the SPC and link the IAM role. i also left an IAM snippet in the PR description.

anya: CI question: does plan/apply still run the same terraform workspace flow? will this change affect tainting/resource replacements?

mike: workflow unchanged. because providers are pinned and modules moved, replacements are minimal. i saw a terraform plan that showed a few resource replacements in state where provider alias changed; i handled those with state mv in the follow-up.

paul: can you paste the state mv snippet? might save me time when i run upgrade on the eu cluster.

mike: sure — in case you need it:
```bash
# move resource using aliased provider
terraform state mv "module.old_module.aws_eks_cluster.cluster" "module.new_module.aws_eks_cluster.cluster"
```
recommend planning with -target first to validate.

jordan: also FYI, i pinned module sources to the registry with digests: source = "app.terraform.io/redwood/modules/infra/k8s/aws?ref=v0.2.1" and added the SHA in the module registry entry so future upgrades will require explicit bump.

talia: 👍 love the explicitness. will this block quick fixes?

jordan: you can still test with a local override or replace provider during dev. prod follows the digest pins. i added a short paragraph on using "terraform init -get-plugins=false" for local iterate.

devops-bot: [deploy] staging plan succeeded for infra/hoist-providers (pipeline #278) :white_check_mark:

anya: one last ask — could we add a smoke test that verifies the CSI mount is present in pods after deploy? simple kubectl get pods -o yaml check.

jordan: good idea, added a small test in the k8s CI job that greps for secretProviderClass in pod volumes.

paul: ok i'll run the eu upgrade tomorrow morning. thx everyone for the quick reviews. :rocket:
